deploy.title: Deploy automatically from GitHub or GitLab
deploy.intro: Every push to your main branch can upload your site here by itself. Set it up once:
deploy.step1: 1. Create a key just for deployments
deploy.step1Hint: Run this on your computer. It makes two files: deploy_key (private) and deploy_key.pub (public). Use a separate key so you can switch deployments off without touching your own access.
deploy.step2Hint: Paste the contents of deploy_key.pub into "Add a key" and give it a label like "GitHub deploy".
deploy.step3: 3. Save the private key in your repository as {secret}
deploy.step3Hint: GitHub: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret. GitLab: Settings → CI/CD → Variables, tick Masked and Protected. Paste the whole contents of deploy_key.
deploy.step4GitHubHint: Your server details are already filled in. Commit the file to main and the first deployment starts.
deploy.step4GitLab: 4. GitLab: add this job to .gitlab-ci.yml instead
deploy.step4GitLabHint: Use this one if your code is on GitLab. Your server details are already filled in.
deploy.step5: 5. To stop deployments, revoke the deploy key in the list above.
